newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels fire on plane over Goma.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels fire on plane over Goma.

text.p: Rebels opened fired with anti-aircraft batteries and machineguns at a plane repeatedly flying over the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Wednesday.
The rebels, saying they suspected it was carrying French troops, blasted at the twin-propeller light plane which made at least three passes over the city.
Explosions could be seen in the sky as the guns blasted towards the aircraft but it was not apparently hit by the fire.
"If French troops arrive in Goma as part of the international intervention force we will fire on them and resist them," Commandant Andre Kassasse, the rebel chief in Goma, told reporters.

Zaire's Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels and the Tutsi-led Rwandan government in Kigali deeply distrust France which for years supported the former Hutu government held responsible for the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 people, mainly Tutsis.

That distrust was further increased after a French-led intervention towards the end of the genocide allowed many Hutu leaders to escape and begin plotting a comeback from refugee camps over the border in eastern Zaire.

"Any international force will be welcome here...Any American troops will be welcome," added the commander, wearing a stolen Zairean army uniform. "We are still discussing security arrangements to be made when the intervention force arrives."
The firing resounded around the city after seven injured Zairean civilians were taken to hospital after being badly trampled in a stampede at a U.N. warehouse filled with biscuits and powdered milk.

More than 2,000 people gathered on Wednesday morning outside the U.N. refugee agency warehouse and lined up but they later stampeded towards the gates and were repulsed by stick-wielding volunteers and rebels.
"We have not been distributing this (food) because we were organising our distribution system and taking medical advice on whether protien biscuits would be good for the population," said Kassasse.

The rebel chief said rebel forces were near Mugunga camp, which is west of Goma and is believed to contain large numbers of Rwandan refugees. Before the rebels seized Goma, it was the largest refugee camp in the world with a population of 400,000.
Kassasse said Mugunga residents were not moving but there had been "some small escapes of women and children" westwards.
"We are waiting for an intervention force to come before we attack Mugunga," he added. The camp is held by exiled Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen who fled to Zaire in 1994 with the refugees.
"The refugees don't concern us but the fact they are armed does."
Kassasse however said rebel forces would not take part in any operation to separate Interahamwe militiamen, who took a leading part in the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, from the refugees.
"The intervention force will not be a police force...We will not be putting any time limit on how long they stay," he said.
He said more than 150 former Zairean troops had surrendered to the rebels, who he said would seize all Zaire from President Mobutu Sese Seko, hold a referendum and then general elections.
